newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 13.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 13.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

LONDON - Advertising executives say there's been a shift in the advertising marketplace, with financial institutions and telecommunications groups spending an increasing amount of money on advertising, while FMCG companies that have traditionally dominated TV commercials in the UK have been cutting back.

OAK BROOK, Illinois - McDonald's Corp says it will launch a promotion tied to Walt Disney Co's release of the animated film "Hercules." The promotion, which features special Happy Meal toys and premiums and Hercules-themed packaging and in-restaurant decor, will run from June 20 through July 24.

MILAN - The public relations business is expected to grow rapidly in Italy, where companies are having to get a grip on communication skills like never before, according to a survey by Shandwick Italia.
But Shandwick Italia says the PR sector also faces big challenges and has to rethink its strategy and purpose because people believed less and less in the media and in advertising.

JOHANNESBURG - Sasani Ltd, a South African entertainment and communication group that recently floated on the stock market, buys a local advertising agency, Msomi Hunt Lascaris, whose clients include Coca Cola and Standard Bank.

WASHINGTON - An attempt by the Federal Communications Commission, the top communications regulator in the U.S., to open a probe into hard-liquor advertising on television was thwarted when two of the FCC's commissioners said the investigation was outside FCC jurisdiction and would be better handled by the Federal Trade Commission.
PARIS - Publicis, the French-based advertising group, expects to make double-digit profit growth 1997, chairman Maurice Levy says.
LONDON - Ogilvy Group Inc, a subsidiary of WPP Group Plc, expands its position in Latin America by buying the outstanding 28 percent of ordinary shares in Ogilvy & Mather Argentina S.A.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

JOHANNESBURG - Bumper advertising revenues and subscription income from its new satellite television service is expected to back a leap in earnings at South African pay-television firm M-Net, according to analysts.

SAN FRANCISCO, California - Online ad revenues surged to $129.5 million in the first quarter of 1997, a rise of more than $20 million, or 18 percent, from record fourth quarter 1996 levels, according to the Internet Advertising Bureau.
PARIS - Jean-Marie Messier, chairman of France's Cie Generale des Eaux, rules out buying TF1, a rival to its indirectly-controlled pay TV unit Canal Plus, according to Liberation newspaper.

BONN - Germany's anti-trust watchdog approves plans by media giant Bertelsmann AG and publishing house Axel Springer Verlag AG to set up a jointly-owned online sports channel called Sportkanal GmbH, Bertelsmann says.

SINGAPORE - Phoning via the Internet is fast and costs a fraction of ordinary international calls, but the quality is still poor and must improve before it will take off, say experts at an Asian telecommunications conference. A senior academic said companies were spending too much time searching for high technology "killer applications", without addressing the fact that the biggest hits so far on the Internet are gambling and pornography, and most high technology is not improving the lives of poor people around the world.
KUALA LUMPUR - Malaysia has signalled the arrival of a freer press by announcing it will withdraw the national news agency's rights to distribute foreign news, analysts say.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

TOKYO - Industry experts say Japanese companies are waking up to the business potential of the African continent three years after Nelson Mandela was elected to head South Africa's first post-apartheid government and are investing to expand market share in southern Africa.

NEW YORK - Financial analysts say a recent report that Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc is planning a price increase may indicate that the price war waged over the last four months by major soft-drink makers in the United States may be ending. *********
LONDON - The planned flotation of motor racing's Formula One Holdings is likely to be delayed until September, sources close to the discussions say.
TAIPEI - Taiwan's Hong Kong-listed Tingyi (Cayman Islands) Holding Corp, which dominates the instant noodle market in China, says it's considering a T$10 billion investment at home in Taiwan.
WASHINGTON - The U.S. House tax writing committee rejects proposal that would have raised taxes on cigarettes by 29 cents per pack to 53 cents.

LONDON - W.H. Smith Group Plc, the UK retail group, is in talks to spin off its U.S. music business, The Wall, as part of a wave of rationalisation in the troubled U.S. sector, the Financial Times newspaper reports.

STUTTGART - Industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG says truck orders rose by over 70 percent in the first five months of 1997. Daimler, Germany's leading truck maker, also says it expects worldwide truck sales to increase by 15 percent for the whole year.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

WELLINGTON - A New Zealander has developed a spray that smells so bad it scares off aggressive dogs. Called "Skunk Shot" because the chemicals used replicate those excreted by a skunk, it works best sprayed in the dog's face. But it's been given the thumbs up by the Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals.

HARARE - Fashion designers will be allowed to continue using the world's finest thread, from the vicuna, a member of the llama family which lives in Latin America, but environmental groups say they want to curb poaching of the animal.
LONDON - A British study has shown that Star Trek fans are like drug addicts who suffer withdrawal symptoms if deprived of their favourite television show.
GENEVA - The World Health Organisation says obesity is now a global epidemic, with excess weight putting the health of millions of people at risk.
PARIS - A newly-elected French Communist deputy says he will wear blue overalls to the first session of parliament to symbolise his working class roots.
